newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Nairn quits as JCI managing director.
newsitem.headline: Nairn quits as JCI managing director.

text.p: South African mining house JCI Ltd, recently taken over by black empowerment consortium African Mining Group (AMG), said on Tuesday that Bill Nairn had agreed to stand down as managing director.
New chairman Mzi Khumalo said the move was effective immediately.
Khumalo said in a statement that the best interests of JCI would be served by Nairn standing down as managing director and that Nairn had agreed to do so.

"With my increasing involvement in the business of the company, it has become clear that there is little reason to maintain both the position of executive chairman and managing director," Khumalo said.
He said the new owners were "well aware" of JCI's good performance since its inception in May 1995.

"At the same time, I wish to recognise that JCI Ltd's success rests on the qulity of the team which Bill Nairn assembled and I reiterate our commitment to retaining the current management," Khumalo added.

Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd and De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd sold a 30 percent stake in JCI to AMG this year -- putting control of one of the country's largest mining houses in the hands of blacks.
Certain members of the AMG consortium have been granted an option over a further 4.9 percent of JCI for one year.
